premises: BMPS arXiv:2603.08664v1 Definitions 2.1-2.4, 2.18-2.31, Remark 2.33 and Lemma 2.34 specify finite globally embedded rational carrying complexes, saturated tangent lattices, rational source weights, primitive inward quotient lifts, continuous literal PA functions with integral linear parts and rational constants, and the tangent-corrected divisor. The whole 2.34 proof is refinement compatibility for such source PA functions and cycles. This is not a source theorem allowing arbitrary actual real coefficients or weights; that extension is separately calibrated.

BMPS arXiv:2603.08664v1 Definitions 3.2-3.3 require rational PCC endpoints in X intersect N_Q, nonnegative real coefficients summing to one, and a center face incident to all endpoint faces; the center need not be rational. The resulting PC class is defined for finite real-valued functions without a continuity or PA restriction. The whole Lemma 3.4 and simplicial Proposition 3.7 were inspected but their equivalence/automatic-continuity claims are not imported as a general theorem for the actual real category.

BMPS arXiv:2603.08664v1 Proposition 3.22 and Definition 3.23 concern a continuous function and uniform/decreasing relative PA regularization for a fixed reference, using the source PA category and compactification in the proof. The audit imports only the source approximation convention; the actual real closure and genuine rational-shift decreasing extraction are independently proved.

BMPS arXiv:2603.08664v1 Definitions 4.4-4.7 define finite atomic raw d-fold primitive intersections and degree without an additional factorial. Lemma 4.6 assumes a bounded PA difference; Proposition 4.8 uses the source PA domain and delegated commutation. Whole Lemmas 4.9 and 4.11 restrict IBP to bounded relevant PA factors and use primitive edge lengths, cancellation on bounded edges and zero bounded-function slopes on unbounded edges. The audit reconstructs these finite identities in its actual real common-carrier domain using BBGS commutation rather than importing the delegated source assertion.

BMPS arXiv:2603.08664v1 Definition 4.15 requires the reference's linear part to be strictly positive on every nonzero vector in each recession cone. The audit tests the finite rational pointed recession generators and independently derives coercivity and properness; no source density theorem follows from this definition.

BMPS arXiv:2603.08664v1 Definition 6.2 takes the unrestricted PC minorant supremum beneath a continuous obstacle plus the reference, with upper bound gamma+O(1). Proposition 6.3 compares envelopes; Theorem 6.4 and Corollaries 6.7-6.8 are source regularity/approximation statements within their hypotheses and literal PA convention. Definition 6.9 explicitly assumes pair-level regularity before the orthogonality property. The audit does not import broad regularity or silently infer actual envelope PA-domain membership from continuity.

BBGS 2022 publisher Definitions 2.1-2.3 and 2.14-2.15 define compatible polyhedral structures and a Euclidean quasi-embedding into an affine hyperplane. A global embedding x mapped to (x,1) with product Euclidean metric satisfies these hypotheses; its cell tangents have last coordinate zero and keep the original tangent metric.

BBGS 2022 publisher Definitions 3.1-3.9 and whole Remark 3.6 permit real k-weights, real continuous cellwise affine functions on a common carrying structure, inward Euclidean unit conormals, and the negative product coefficient -sum c_sigma f_sigma(v_sigma/tau). Signed and zero weights are allowed. This product is the source operation converted by B_-f(ac)(tau)=a_tau D_f c(tau), not an ambient Alexandrov measure.

BBGS 2022 publisher Proposition 3.12 states and proves product compatibility with restriction and subdivision for real PA functions and real weights on a common Euclidean quasi-embedded complex. Its whole subdivision proof treats inherited codimension-one faces, new facets of old weighted cells with equal opposite conormals, and faces whose old dimension is larger and thus have zero inherited weight. Strict positivity and simpliciality are not required.

BBGS 2022 publisher Proposition 3.15 states and proves f dot (g dot c)=g dot (f dot c) for two real PA functions carried by the same Euclidean complex and a real k-weight c, k>=2. In its whole proof an actual codimension-two quotient wedge has two facets; reflected oriented unit-perpendicular expansions give symmetric diagonal terms and paired cross terms. The equality applies to signed and zero weights and is sign-compatible with using -f,-g in the raw conversion.

BBGS 2022 publisher Lemma 3.18 characterizes a Minkowski weight by vanishing product with every ambient linear form. Proposition 3.19 proves preservation of Minkowski weights under restriction, subdivision and real PA products. Its product step uses the commutation equality of 3.15, although the printed citation says 3.12. These whole elementary proofs establish balanced preservation without delegated AR10 commutation.

BBGS 2022 publisher Definition 4.6 distinguishes PA concavity against all positive Minkowski cycles from weak concavity against the specified balancing condition. Definition 5.1 allows arbitrary real endpoints in PCCs, unlike BMPS's rational-endpoint convention. Whole Proposition 5.7 and Proposition 5.10 compare these real-endpoint notions with PA cycle positivity and facewise ordinary concavity. Whole Lemma 6.1 and Theorem 6.2 prove continuity in this real-endpoint balanced setting. The audit inspects this distinction but imports none of these results as printed-rational-PC automatic continuity or higher-dimensional PA approximation.
